correctness.rationale: The full repulsive map is exactly gradient descent for |Z|²/2. A direct parity sign argument proves λmin(JJᵀ)≥1−|Z| for every odd N; combined with hN<1 and the exponential Taylor remainder it proves a closed |Z|≤1/2 invariant basin and rate 1−h/4, plus summable phase increments. Substitution proves the even invariant scalar map and monotonic approach to zero. Expansion of inverse square yields Δy=2h+(3h²−h/2)/y+O(y^-2); summable correction yields the full logarithmic asymptotic and finite constant. The finite verifier is independent support, not the proof.

value.rationale: For the very natural all-to-all repulsive sine map, the balance manifold has a genuine parity-dependent dynamical dichotomy: a dimension-free explicit exponential neighborhood at odd N versus arbitrarily nearby algebraic (and log-corrected) trajectories for every even N. This resolves a substantive infinite-family relaxation question, not a routine finite enumeration or arbitrary parameter slice. The coefficient cancellation h=1/6 adds a nontrivial dynamical step-size effect within the smallest admissible even size.
